paragraphs: Buna bar Shila: [Jerusalem Talmud Gittin, chapter 2, halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Gittin.2.3.6).

Rav Yitzchak bar Shila: Kiddushin 32 (supplied .:; compare [Davidson 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.32a.15)). Natan bar Shila: Chullin 58 (supplied .:; compare [Davidson 58b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.58b.8)). Rava bar Shila: [Shabbat 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.63a.18). Rabbah bar Shila: Berakhot 2 (supplied .:; compare [Davidson 2b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.2b.2)). Ravina bar Shila: [Sukkah 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.13a.4).

notes.text: The supplied .: punctuation leaves the sides at Kiddushin 32, Chullin 58 and Berakhot 2 unsettled. Unsupported a sides have been removed. The clear Shabbat 63a and Sukkah 13a locators remain. The affected p004 stays held.

The supplied Kiddushin 32, Chullin 58 and Berakhot 2 references each have conflicting .: side marks. Fresh Davidson comparisons locate Rav Yitzchak bar Shila at Kiddushin 32a, Natan bar Shila at Chullin 58b, and Rabbah bar Rav Shila at Berakhot 2b. These corresponding locators are displayed as named-edition comparisons beside the original .: marks in the English; they do not replace the supplied punctuation. Berakhot has the additional Rav in the patronymic; the supplied Rabbah bar Shila is not silently changed. The clear Shabbat 63a and Sukkah 13a references remain. The cause and exact printed form of the double marks remain unresolved.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. III, p. 1111) also shows both side marks at Kiddushin 32, Chullin 58 and Berakhot 2. The reason for the double marks is unclear. The consulted Shabbat 63a gives Rava bar Rav Shila as one of two alternative transmitters. The consulted Shabbat 139a–b has Rabbi Yehudah bar Shilat in Rabbi Assi’s name. In Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 2:3, the consulted Hebrew text reads Bina Shiluach, the Guggenheimer English reads Bina bar Shila, and the Vilna-based exposition on Daat reads Buna bar Shila. Hyman also proposes Shila bar Buna under a separate heading (p. 1113). These variants leave the identities open.
